# Sigma Support

RASD evaluates and converts a defined subset of the Sigma specification with its own engine (`tools/sigma_engine.py`) and converter (`tools/convert.py`). Anything outside the subset raises an error: no rule is evaluated or converted approximately. Rule files use standard Sigma syntax only; contracts, tuning guides and tests live beside them.

Every row is checked on each build by `tools/sigma_support.py`: a supported construct gives the same verdict in the engine, the compiled engine and the generated SPL and KQL (run by RASD's interpreters of each language) on 7 probe events (exact and other case, look-alikes, wildcards, empty and missing fields, a multi-line value), and a refused construct raises an error in all four.

## Supported

| Construct | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Plain value | equality, case-insensitive |
| Wildcards `*` and `?` | any run of characters / exactly one character, nothing else is special |
| Value list | any value matches (OR) |
| `contains` `startswith` `endswith` | substring, prefix, suffix; case-insensitive |
| `all` | every value of the list must match (AND) |
| `cased` | case-sensitive match, with any of the above |
| `re` | regular expression search, case-sensitive unless the pattern starts with `(?i)` |
| `re` with `i` `m` `s` | ignore case, multi-line anchors, dot matches a newline |
| `exists` | `true`: present and not empty; `false`: missing or empty |
| `null` | the field is missing or empty |
| Map selection | every field must match (AND) |
| List of maps | any map matches (OR) |
| `and` `or` `not`, parentheses | boolean condition over selections |
| `1 of` / `all of` a pattern, `them` | quantifiers over selections named by a wildcard |
| A list of conditions | any condition matches (OR) |

Modifiers: `all`, `cased`, `contains`, `endswith`, `exists`, `re`, `startswith`, and `i`, `m`, `s` with `re`. Regular expressions must also be RE2-safe for Sentinel (no lookarounds, backreferences, possessive quantifiers or atomic groups); `rasd lint` checks it.

## Refused

| Construct | Why |
|---|---|
| `base64` `base64offset` `utf16le` `utf16be` `utf16` `wide` | encoded search values |
| `windash` | dash variants: the rules spell out `-`, `/` and the Unicode dashes instead |
| `cidr` | network ranges |
| `expand` | placeholders |
| `fieldref` | field-to-field comparison |
| `gt` `gte` `lt` `lte` | numeric comparison |
| `i` `m` `s` without `re` | regex flags on a non-regex value |
| Aggregation in a condition | `\| count() by ...` was removed in Sigma v2: write a correlation rule |
| `timeframe` in a detection | belongs to the removed aggregations: write a correlation rule |
| A condition that is not a string | only strings and lists of strings are conditions |
| The escapes `\*` `\?` `\\` in a value | Sigma reads them as escapes and RASD would read every backslash literally, so one value would mean two things: write single backslashes (`\127.0.0.1\` finds a UNC path), or use `re` |
| Wildcards inside `contains` `startswith` `endswith` | Sigma expands them there and RASD would compare them literally: split the value, or use `re` |

## Evaluated offline, not converted

| Construct | Why |
|---|---|
| Keyword selection | a bare list of plain strings (no wildcards or escapes) searched in every field: write a field condition to deploy it |

## Correlation rules

Types `event_count` and `value_count` over one base rule, with `group-by`, a `timespan` of whole minutes that divide an hour (or whole hours that divide a day), and one condition: `gte`, `gt`, `lte`, `lt`, `eq`. `temporal`, `temporal_ordered` and any other type are refused (`tests/test_correlation.py`). Proofs: [CORRELATIONS](CORRELATIONS.md).

## Numbers

A number in a rule is compared as a number in SPL and KQL. Quote it when the column is text, as the web rules do for status codes (`sc-status: '401'`).
